items.title: Does forcing one shared definition actually stay cheaper as more teams get involved?
items.description: An illustrative model, not a precise estimate for any real organization. A pair means two teams compared together: Billing-Support is one pair, Billing-Sales would be another. Forcing every team onto one shared definition means many pairs need their assumptions reconciled against each other, which grows fast as teams are added. Bounded contexts are simplified here as roughly one maintained boundary per team to show the pattern, not every real context-map relationship.
items.compute: const sharedModelConflicts = Math.round(params.numTeams * (params.numTeams - 1) / 2); const boundedContextBoundaries = params.numTeams; return { sharedModelConflicts, boundedContextBoundaries };

outputs.label: Pairwise conflicts to reconcile (one shared definition)
